백재윤은 모니터 구석의 계산기 창을 끄지 않았다. 동접 20만이면 후원 800. 30만이면 천이 넘는다. 광고 수익은 따로다. 채널 역대 최고 기록은 27만이었다. 오늘은 넘는다.
"조건은 7 대 3."
서아는 대기실 소파 끝에 앉아 있었다. 회색 후드 소매가 손가락을 반쯤 덮었다. 그 안에서 엄지가 검지 손톱 옆 살을 뜯었다.
"누가 7인데."
"내가. 장비, 편집, 송출, 소송 리스크. 다 내 거야."
"네가 피고석에 앉는 거."
서아가 고개를 들었다. 오빠와 닮은 가는 눈이 재윤의 얼굴을 한 번 훑고, 모니터로 갔다가, 다시 돌아왔다.
"기사 한 줄 나오는 데 한 달이야. 경찰은 몇 달이고. 그동안 넌 매일 욕먹어. 난 오늘 밤에 끝내. 넌 피해자 되고, 난 역대 조회수. 윈윈이잖아."
"오빠는 나 살리려는 거야, 팔려는 거야?"
재윤은 대답 대신 새로고침을 눌렀다. 대기 인원 4만 2천.
"둘 다. 둘 다 되는 게 제일 잘 팔려."
서아는 대답하지 않았다. 손톱 옆에 피가 조금 비쳤다. 서아는 그 손을 소매 안으로 밀어 넣었다.

plan.intent: A quiet pre-show negotiation that plays like a contract signing. The reader should feel the gap between what Jaeyun watches and what he misses. He watches his numbers: the calculator window, the waiting count. He misses his sister's hand, which is quietly hurting itself inside her sleeve. The hum of the air conditioner is the only loud thing in the room. Each of his lines closes a deal. Each of her lines tests whether she is being rescued or sold. His honest answer, 'both', lands at the same moment as a rising viewer number. The scene ends in her silence and a small hidden wound he never looks at. That wound is the real event, and it sits outside anything his camera would catch.

beats.action: The basement studio is established before airtime. The air conditioner hum dominates. Jaeyun sits at his monitor with the calculator window still open, running projections and settling on the certainty that tonight breaks the record.
Jaeyun names the terms of the deal. The line belongs to him: he opens the negotiation.
Seoa, at the end of the sofa, is picking at her finger inside her sleeve. She asks who gets the larger share.
Jaeyun claims the 7 and lists everything he carries.
Seoa prompts for the rest. Jaeyun names her part: the defendant's seat.
Seoa lifts her head. Her gaze goes from his face to the monitor and back, reading what he actually wants.
Jaeyun makes the speed argument (slow press and police against tonight's show) and closes it as a win-win.
Seoa asks directly whether he is saving her or selling her.
Instead of answering, Jaeyun refreshes. The waiting count reads 42 thousand.
Jaeyun answers after all: both, because both sells best.
Seoa gives no reply. Blood shows faintly beside her nail, and she tucks the hand into her sleeve. The wound is hidden, not displayed.

facts.statement: It is twenty minutes before the broadcast, in a basement studio in Mangwon-dong. The air conditioner is the only loud sound.

Jaeyun keeps a calculator window open in a corner of his monitor. He estimates donations of 800 at 200k concurrent viewers and over a thousand at 300k, with ad revenue separate. The source gives no unit for these amounts. The channel's all-time record is 270k, and he is sure tonight will beat it.
The deal is a 7-to-3 split. Jaeyun takes the 7, citing equipment, editing, streaming and litigation risk as all his.
Seoa sits at the end of the waiting-room sofa. The sleeves of her grey hoodie half cover her fingers. Inside the sleeve, her thumb picks at the skin beside her index fingernail.
Seoa's side of the deal is to sit in the defendant's seat on the show.
Seoa looks up. Her narrow eyes, like her brother's, pass once over Jaeyun's face, go to the monitor, then come back. From where she sits, both his face and the monitor are within her view.
Jaeyun's pitch: the press takes a month and the police take months, while she gets abused every day. He will finish it tonight. She becomes the victim, he gets record views.
Instead of answering her question, Jaeyun presses refresh. The waiting audience count shows 42 thousand.
Seoa does not answer. A little blood shows beside her fingernail, and she pushes that hand into her sleeve.

units.text: "대표님, 화살표요."
콘솔 쪽에서 윤채리가 헤드셋을 한쪽 귀에만 걸친 채 불렀다. 썸네일 시안에는 서아의 옆얼굴과 흐릿한 교복 영상 캡처가 나란히 있었고, 그 사이를 빨간 화살표 세 개가 갈랐다.
"세 개는 과해요. 조작 냄새 난다고 해요."
"두 개면 성의 없어 보여."
"세 개면 싸 보이고요." 채리가 뿔테를 밀어 올렸다. "그리고 공유 폴더에 final_무죄 올려놨어요. 원본 대조, 입 모양 어긋나는 구간 슬로모션까지. 6분 12초."
재윤은 폴더를 열었다. final_무죄.mp4. 미리보기 프레임에는 반 박자 늦게 벌어지는 입이 멈춰 있었다. 사흘 밤을 깎은 영상이었다. 없는 건 하나도 안 넣었다. 있는 걸 순서대로 놓았을 뿐이다.
그는 판결 설정 화면으로 넘어갔다.

[판결 LIVE — 형량 설정]
시청자 투표 게이지 100% 도달 시 자동 실행
☑ 피고 신상 공개 게시물 자동 업로드
규칙은 단순했다. 시청자가 '유죄'를 누를수록 게이지가 찬다. 100%가 되면 미리 걸어 둔 형량이 사람 손을 거치지 않고 실행된다. 그래서 시청자는 진짜 판사처럼 누르고, 방송은 진짜 사형장처럼 팔린다.
"신상 공개요?" 채리의 목소리가 낮아졌다. "동생분 걸로요?"
"무죄잖아. 안 차."
"그럼 왜 거는데요."
"형량이 세야 뒤집힐 때 터지지."
채리는 더 말하지 않았다. 타임코드 창을 열었다가 닫았다. 재윤이 확인을 눌렀다. 초록색 체크가 떴다.
예약 완료.

plan.intent: A routine pre-show work exchange turns into a sentencing, and nobody raises their voice. The scene opens on trivia: how many red arrows a thumbnail should carry. The same flat, businesslike rhythm then carries the reader into the verdict settings screen, where the armed punishment is identity exposure of Jaeyun's own sister. Jaeyun is proud that he added nothing false to the video. That pride makes him certain the gauge cannot fill. The certainty lets him arm the device anyway, because a heavy sentence makes the reversal louder. Cheri is the only person in the room who registers the weight. Her voice drops, then she stops talking and opens and closes a timecode window, a small nervous action beside the real click. The decisive event should feel small, quiet and irreversible: a finger on a confirm button and a green check, set up while Jaeyun believes nothing can go wrong. His line in ch-1-p-25 is left standing, uncorrected.

plan.intent: The live show opens, and the performance is louder than anything else in the room. Jaeyun fires his catchphrase under hot light with a grin that is too wide. The concurrent-viewer counter is already six figures, and he casually tells the audience that tonight's defendant is his own sister, as if it were a twist he is proud of. The chat erupts with delight at the family betrayal. Then the scene's weight moves off the host and onto the four white-lit steps between the edge of the set and the defendant chair. Seoa is summoned. She grips the camera strap at her neck once, lets go, walks, and sits. Her greeting is small and trails in. Her name alone pushes the guilty gauge past half, and the reader knows from the previous scene that at 100% her identity exposure fires automatically. Jaeyun does not register any of this as danger. He treats the anger as a warm-up, raises one finger, promises a reversal in three minutes, and calls for playback. The reader should feel the gap between his certainty and the number that is already climbing, and between his broadcast voice and his sister's silent hand on the strap.

plan.intent: The promised three-minute reversal detonates the wrong way. The screen blinks black, and instead of the exculpatory edit Jaeyun spent three nights cutting, a clean, sharp, sound-on clip plays. A girl in a school uniform laughs at the end of a corridor while another kid is shoved toward the wall and slides down. Then she turns to face the camera, and there is a mole under her right eye, the same mark the reader knows is on Seoa, who is sitting in the defendant chair a few steps away. The reader should feel the floor drop out before anyone on set says what happened. Jaeyun's showman patter is gone. He manages only a bare name toward the console. What comes back through his in-ear is breath first, then Cheri insisting the file name was right, that she is the one who played it, and reading timecodes aloud as if counting could hold the clip still. Meanwhile the numbers keep doing their job without him. The guilty gauge climbs, the chat moves faster than eyes can read, the viewers mock the 'innocence evidence' and cheer the brother for exposing his own sister, and the concurrent-viewer count swells far past where the show began. The scene ends on the audience growing, not on any explanation. The gap is between what Jaeyun meant to air and what his own broadcast is now sentencing her with.

plan.intent: The reversal has already landed; this scene is about what Jaeyun does with his body while the verdict machine runs on without him. He reaches for his usual on-air voice, gets out the opening words, and nothing follows. Just then the one person in the room who reads fakes the way he reads edits leans forward from the defendant chair, squints at the monitor, and starts to name a flaw. She stops mid-word, and he does not ask. His eyes are already on a number. From there the numbers carry the scene: the guilty gauge climbs in steps, viewers pour in, donations cheer the judge for being fair and demand the sentence be carried out. His thumb keeps hitting refresh, the count keeps rising, and an all-time record passes without a sound. The ethical weight sits below frame. Under the desk his right hand comes down over the red-rimmed end-broadcast button, stops short, and does not touch it. His reasoning arrives as cold arithmetic, not remorse: 300k is close, the clip is already out, and quitting now leaves one damning line about him fleeing. The scene closes on the gauge at 97, with the hand still hovering and nothing resolved. The gap the reader should feel: his sister offered the thread that could clear her, and he let it drop to watch a counter.

plan.intent: Continuation of the same night, after outside control seized the broadcast. Jaeyun tries to undo the sentence he set up. The machine refuses him. His own PD cannot help. With nothing left to press, his body falls back on its habit: refresh, refresh. The stream is dead and live viewers read zero, yet the clip of what just happened sits at the top of the popular list, and its count climbs while he watches. Meanwhile the real event happens outside the screen he is staring at. A chair scrapes. His sister is on her feet and walking. She does not stop this time, and she does not come toward him. The reader sees only her grey-hooded back moving to the stairwell. When he finally speaks to her, his first sentence is about views, cut off mid-word, and he never corrects it. The only answer is the sound of the iron door closing at the top of the stairs. The emotional gap: he holds numbers while the person leaves, and his distance to her is measured in her steps, not his. Two readings here are interpretation, not source fact: that he stays at the desk, and that the door's sound lands over an emptied set.

He turns to Seoa and calls. It rings eight times and cuts off. He calls again, and it cuts off after six. He puts the phone face down on the desk, which is a physical withdrawal from her silence.

Under pressure, his mind escapes into numbers, framed as subtitles like on his own broadcasts. The rent debt, the ad penalties and the best-case donations from the 1,840 viewers never add up. The calculation keeps landing in the same place.
The phone he turned face down shudders on the desk. Something has arrived, though not what he was waiting for.

units.text: "서아 방에서 찍은 거 있지. 사전 인터뷰."
채리의 손이 잠깐 멈췄다. "……전부 있어요."
사흘 전, 서아의 원룸에서 찍은 원본이었다. 방송에는 한 프레임도 안 나간 영상이었다. 채리가 외장 SSD를 꽂자 폴더가 열렸다.

화면 속 방은 좁았다. 이불이 반듯하게 개어져 있었고, 책상 위에는 고양이가 그려진 머그컵이 놓여 있었다. 서아는 카메라 밖의 누군가를 보며 뭔가 말하고 있었다. 소리는 꺼져 있었다. 그녀 뒤쪽 창밖으로 맞은편 건물이 보였다. 간판 글자가 반쯤 잘려 있었고, 초록색 십자 모양이 걸려 있었다. 현관 신발장 위에는 택배 상자가 있었고, 송장 한 귀퉁이가 카메라 쪽을 향해 있었다.
채리의 커서가 창문 위에서 멈췄다.
되감았다. 다시 재생했다. 또 되감았다.
세 번째 되감기 끝에 그녀가 고개를 돌렸다.
"간판이랑 송장이요. 블러 걸까요, 대표님? 어느 쪽으로 하셔도 제 손은 금방 가요."
재윤은 화면을 봤다. 머그컵을 봤다. 개어 둔 이불도 봤다. 서아는 원래 이불을 개지 않는 애였다. 방송 찍는다고 갠 것이었다.
삼 초쯤 그렇게 봤다.
"현장감." 그가 말했다. "흐리면 짜 맞춘 걸로 보여."
채리는 아무 말도 하지 않았다. 커서가 창문에서 내려와 [렌더] 버튼 위로 갔다. 딸깍, 소리가 났다. 진행 바가 차오르기 시작했다. 재윤은 휴대폰을 뒤집어 서아에게 한 번 더 전화를 걸었다. 신호가 가다가 끊겼다.
다시 엎었다.

beats.action: Jaeyun asks for the pre-interview footage from Seoa's room. Chaeri's working hand stops for a moment before she confirms they have everything. This is the first small hesitation.
The SSD goes in and the folder opens. Narration marks what is at stake: raw material from three days ago that has never been broadcast.

Seoa's silent room plays on the monitor. It shows the folded blanket, the cat mug and Seoa talking to someone off-frame. Behind her are the half-cut sign with the green cross and the parcel label corner facing the lens.
Chaeri's cursor freezes on the window. She rewinds and replays, murmuring timecodes as the same seconds loop. Her anxiety shows through repetition, not words.
After the third rewind Chaeri turns to Jaeyun and puts the choice in his hands. Blur the sign and label or not; she can do either fast.
Jaeyun's gaze moves across the screen to the mug and the folded blanket. The narration supplies what only a brother knows: she folded it for the camera. Three seconds of looking pass.
The decision: Jaeyun chooses realism over blur, arguing that blur reads as fabrication. The sentence stands; nobody corrects it.

Chaeri says nothing, moves the cursor off the window and clicks render, and the progress bar starts filling. At the same time Jaeyun calls Seoa again. The call rings and drops, and he turns the phone face down. The scene ends on the filling bar and the dead phone.

facts.statement: Someone asks whether they have the pre-interview footage shot in Seoa's room. The line carries no speaker tag. Context implies Jaeyun, because Chaeri answers and later addresses him as boss.
Chaeri's hand pauses briefly before she answers, with a trailing hesitation, that they have all of it.
The footage is raw original material shot three days earlier in Seoa's one-room studio apartment. Not a single frame of it has aired. Chaeri plugs in an external SSD and a folder opens.

On screen, the room is small. The blanket is neatly folded, and a mug with a cat drawn on it sits on the desk. Seoa is saying something while looking at someone outside the camera frame. The sound is off.

Through the window behind Seoa, the building opposite is visible. Its sign lettering is cut roughly in half, and a green cross shape hangs there. A parcel box sits on the shoe cabinet by the entrance, with one corner of its shipping label facing the camera.
Chaeri's cursor stops over the window. She rewinds, plays again and rewinds again, reading the timecodes quietly aloud (text-7, text-8). After the third rewind she turns her head toward Jaeyun.
Chaeri names the sign and the shipping label and asks her boss whether to blur them. She adds that either way her hands will be quick.
Jaeyun looks at the screen, then the mug, then the folded blanket. Narration states that Seoa normally never folds her blanket and folded it because she was filming. He looks for about three seconds.
Jaeyun answers with one word for on-site realism, then says that blurring would make it look staged.
Chaeri says nothing. Her cursor moves down from the window to the render button, a click sounds and a progress bar begins to fill.
Jaeyun flips his phone over and calls Seoa once more. The call rings, then cuts off. He turns the phone face down again.

plan.intent: Chapter 2, same basement studio. The sleepless night has turned into early morning, and Jaeyun goes live to take back the broadcast that was hijacked. That body work is the part no viewer sees. Then he performs. He bends his signature opening to fit the hour: the lawless night has come in the morning. He recasts himself from 'just a camera' to 'the camera that got robbed', which is the same blame-shifting defense in new clothes. He turns a mocking donation into a boast about his no-fabrication principle and plays the evidence. The file keeps the name shown in text-13, but something entirely different plays, slowed to half speed. The scene's pulse is the concurrent-viewer counter climbing in three steps while the chat speeds up and opinion tilts toward him. He closes by naming the mystery as today's case: same label, different contents, and who swapped them. The tone is cold and bright, a confident voice over a body that had to be wound up. Nothing is resolved.

plan.intent: Chapter 2, same basement studio, the same live broadcast that the previous scene left climbing. Jaeyun has been fluent until now. He cuts to his sister's room and says one flat line, and then his broadcast voice fails. For a held beat the event is not on the screen. It is in the man who stops talking in front of 18,400 people while a sign outside her window drifts across the middle of the frame. The black comedy is structural. His silence is the moment the counter reads highest so far, and the one unscripted pause earns an audience. He restarts a beat late with the claim that the room footage took three days to make and was not what aired. After that he is back in his competence zone. The admin screen, the greyed cancel button and the unknown nickname come easily, and when he enlarges the nickname capture the donations explode. The crowd snaps straight back into verdict mode: find the culprit, and where do we vote him innocent. The counter jumps again. The reader should feel the gap between the stalled body and the racing numbers. Nothing about the hijacker is resolved, and nothing future is foreshadowed beyond what the source puts on screen.

Per production direction, the signboard outside that window is a pharmacy sign cut off by the window frame, showing a green cross. plan.intent: Jaeyun reaches the room he came for and finds it already emptied. The pursuit from the street ends at a door that has always stuck a hand's width open. The narration ties that door to his own visit with filming gear three days earlier. He calls his sister once and gets no answer. The reader then takes stock of the room with him: things folded, removed or turned away. The folded blanket, the six empty hangers, the missing toothbrush, the dust-free rectangle where the external drive sat and the chair still angled toward the window as it was for his interview all point to a departure the source never narrates. Seoa is present only as absence. The turn comes from a tablet that lights up by itself and shows that a complaint was filed under her name. The narration then drops the scene's sharpest fact: it was filed seventeen minutes ago. The scene shows where Jaeyun stands and what the room holds. It does not state what he feels, why Seoa left, or where she went. It ends on the time gap, not on his reaction.

plan.intent: The room has already told Jaeyun that Seoa is gone. Now the phone in his hand confirms it three times, each more final than the last. First, the unread chat and the powered-off call. Second, the sibling cloud where she has left. Third, one remaining folder he cannot open. The reader follows his thumb rather than his face. He refreshes and refreshes again, and the gesture shows his habit of treating a screen as something that can be pulled until it changes. The shared folder carries a name Seoa gave it as a middle schooler. Its contents, the family's photos, contracts and their mother's hospital receipts, have turned grey and empty. That makes her exit personal and domestic, not technical. The scene ends on a truncated folder name and a flat refusal, with the spinner stopping. It gives no explanation of what the folder is and no reaction shot that interprets it. Nothing on the phone ever answers him.
